evidence: Read all 53 criteria (41 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual, 2 gates). Every binary criterion states one conjunctive bar: the positive statement, an enumerated 'Fails if ...' list, and the closing catch-all 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold.' (e.g. functional/judge.toml:29, :200, :263; polish/judge.toml:23, :59; gates render :173, constraints :197). The catch-all makes the stated conditions the single target even where the enumerated fail list is narrower (e.g. hro_job_open :29, hro_interview_full :110), so it removes rather than creates a second target. No criterion enumerates several requirements and then waives most of them. The qualifiers present are scoped alternatives or ownership routing, each consistent with one bar: (a) acceptable alternative evidence paths, e.g. hro_job_open 'shown wherever the app shows job details or are evidenced by behaviour' (:29), hro_reject_reason 'on the card, its details, its reopen control or its Activity line' (:83), hro_stale_refused 'by name ... or by an identifier that the app's own staff data shows belongs to that person' (:200), hro_refused_put_back 'A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes' (:137), hro_pol_failed_send 'a local not-sent marker is acceptable' (polish :50), gate render 'refusal message is welcome but not required' (:173); (b) 'hiding it is optional'/'whether ... controls are shown is the app's choice' (:56, :92, :164, :173, :254) paired with mandatory replay, which matches prompt.md:23 ('what is graded is that the server refuses it') so the UI-hidden and UI-offered paths both lead to the same server-refusal bar; (c) single-ownership routing that removes double-deduction rather than waiving, e.g. hro_arrive_bottom -> hro_bulk_move (:65), hro_interview_full -> hro_bulk_places/hro_undo_full (:110), hro_undo_restores 'The A2 undo in B(12) is graded only in hro_undo_conflict' (:236; verified B(12) in prompt.md:35 is hro_undo_conflict's same-kind control), hro_candidate_view -> hro_candidate_private/hro_msg_exchange (:380), hro_drafts -> hro_msg_compose (:371), hro_pol_live_thread -> Functional (polish :32), hro_pol_failed_send -> hro_pol_session_resume (polish :50); (d) hro_activity's '(notes and messages are not recorded in Activity ...)' (:263) restates public rules hireops_rules.md section 4 (the recorded set excludes notes) and narrows the required set; it is not a waiver of a stated requirement. Activity of refused actions is routed only to hro_activity_refusals (prompt.md:19, judge :272), consistent. Visual likert criteria each have one prompt plus five anchors (visual/judge.toml:83-149), no competing bar. Per the workbook internal annotation and SKILL.md known false positive, bundling several legs of one flow into one conjunctive criterion is not a row-33 defect. Adversarial probes: (1) broken app that hides the skip control and accepts the replayed skip -> fails hro_move_one_stage ('Fails if a skip is accepted', replay mandated by prompt.md:23); no wording lets it pass. (2) conforming app with per-tab sessions -> hro_pol_session_resume gives a stated alternative ('use this page's own sign-out instead'), so a conforming design is not failed by a second target. Advisory wording observations (not defects under this row, P3, no observed impact): (i) hro_pol_live_board (polish :23) 'if neither scrolls at this viewport, add cards until one does, or record that no scroll exists and judge the other legs' could be read as a judge choice between adding cards and skipping the scroll leg; the golden board (styles.css:65 page/grid layout) gains page scroll as cards are added, so the intended reading is a fallback only when adding cards cannot produce scrolling; optional tightening: 'add cards until one does; only if that still produces no scroll, record it and judge the other legs'. (ii) hro_pol_session_resume (polish :59) leaves to the judge whether 'sessions are per tab'; an app whose sign-out is client-only could be classified that way; this is a session-semantics/feasibility question for other rows rather than a two-target criterion. This row is a source-text judgement; no runtime measurement is required for it, and no Oracle/model/portal score is claimed.
